instruction: Switch to the 'LLM Powered Autonomous Agents' blog article tab in Chrome.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to download 2 blog articles as PDFs to /home/user/Documents/Blog. Successfully created the Blog directory, used Ctrl+P print dialog, navigated save dialogs, saved both PDFs, and switched between Chrome tabs. Failed because PDF filenames included Chrome's default suffix.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use terminal to create directories, navigate Chrome tabs by clicking tab headers, use Ctrl+P print dialog, interact with file save dialogs
metadata.failure_analysis: Model saved PDFs with Chrome's default title format including ' _ Lil'Log' suffix. The evaluator script likely expected filenames matching just the article titles.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed original task into a tab-switching sub-task. The model demonstrated ability to switch between Chrome tabs in the trajectory (clicked on first tab to save the second PDF).
metadata.explanation: Task requires switching to the 'LLM Powered Autonomous Agents' tab. The initial state has the second tab ('Thinking about High-Quality Human Data') active. Evaluator checks the active URL matches the expected blog post URL using active_url_from_accessTree getter and is_expected_active_tab metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (active_url_from_accessTree) correctly extracts the active tab URL from the accessibility tree, which is exactly what's needed to verify tab switching.
Metric (is_expected_active_tab) correctly receives the rules dict directly (type='url', url=...) and compares URLs using compare_urls. Parameter handling follows the framework convention.
Expected URL (https://lilianweng.github.io/posts/2023-06-23-agent/) correctly matches the 'LLM Powered Autonomous Agents' blog post opened in config.
Complete coverage: the single instruction requirement (switch to the correct tab) is fully verified by checking the active tab URL.
Config properly sets up two tabs so the task is meaningful - agent must switch from the second tab to the first.
